finding: Mutation survived: changing the identity checks `is not self.moderator` (resolver.py:265, :279) to value comparison `!=` leaves all tests green. Every test gives the clashing moderator role a value different from the added one, so the identity-versus-equality choice the delta introduced is unpinned.
why: The delta's switch from `!=` to `is not` changes behaviour when a user role is value-identical to the added moderator, and no test would notice a revert.
fix: Add a case where a pattern defines a `moderator` role with the same model, lifespan, count and charter text as the added one, and assert the refusal (or the intended acceptance).
evidence: resolver.py:265 `if MODERATOR in self.roles and self.roles[MODERATOR] is not self.moderator:` replaced by `!=` -> 108 passed (baseline equal); resolver.py:279 `if known is self.moderator and fields is not self.moderator:` replaced by `known == ... and fields != ...` -> 108 passed

finding: test_a_role_named_like_the_added_moderator_is_refused_naming_both now checks two behaviours (include clash, own-moderator clash) in one body by reassigning `saved` and calling refused twice. The second assert checks only 'takes the name', not the 'naming both' the test title promises.
why: A failure of the first scenario hides the second, and the name no longer says which scenario fails.
fix: Split into two tests or parametrize on (saved, expected substrings), and assert the step and pattern in the second case too.
evidence: `message = refused(tmp_path, "p", saved=saved)` ... `saved = {"p": pattern(...)}` ... `assert "role moderator of pattern p takes the name" in refused(tmp_path, "p", saved=saved)`

finding: Mutation survived: `self.added = self.added or (pattern, step)` changed to `self.added = (pattern, step)` (last debate step wins instead of first) passes the suite. Only one debate step exists in the clash tests, so the 'first debate step' the delta's message names in merge-time refusals is unpinned.
why: The refusal message names the step where the moderator was added, and nothing proves it is the first one.
fix: Add a clash case with two hubless debate steps in different patterns and assert the message names the first step.
evidence: resolver.py:270 `self.added = self.added or (pattern, step)` -> mutated `self.added = (pattern, step)` -> 108 passed (baseline equal)
